- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < 0.0) over recent days, reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for downward pressure.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecasted decline, cap the peak at 1.5x recent high to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (e.g., >10% gap), check if sentiment was positive recently — if so, reduce forecast by 3–7% for next period.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates by 5–10% over 30-day horizon, apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to next forecast, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment is positive but price drops sharply, assume mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with 10–15% of recent low, not full swing.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is below 70% of forecast, consider sentiment lag — if sentiment was positive 3–5 days ago, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect delayed reaction.
